Slice Lab

Deep-sea fishing needs a yes or no from the studio after 10 weeks. Six systems, four big questions. Choose how the team builds (every system halfway, or one dive end to end), at what quality, and which dive, then see what's playable at week 10 and which questions still have no answer.

Ten weeks, one decision. Goal: something playable at week 10, and all four questions answered on the real device, so no known surprise is left for production.

Lesson 073: leading a vertical slice

    What this shows

    Halfway everywhere is nowhere

    Six systems at 50% can't be played, measured or judged. The studio decides on slides.

    A slice answers questions

    One dive, every system working together, shows whether it's fun, whether it fits the frame, and what content really costs.

    Pick the hardest slice

    The easy dive proves what nobody doubted and gives a cost per minute that's too low. The trench at night tests the risks.

    This lab is a model, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 073's numbers: 6 systems, 10 weeks. Four questions and what a wrong guess costs if found in production: is it fun (0, it is, with a longer oxygen timer), does darkness lighting fit the handheld frame (no: 16 team-weeks), does depth streaming hitch (yes: 10), what does a minute of dive cost to make (5 artist-weeks, not 2: 20). Grey boxes answer fun; the trench in grey boxes also answers streaming. Final quality answers content cost (wrongly, 2 weeks a minute, on the sunny reef) and, in the trench, handheld lighting. Playable minutes: 8 grey reef, 6 grey trench, 4 final reef, 3 final trench.
